assumptions: Tables patients, appointments and clinical_notes hold PHI; users, orgs and invoices-side tables are not PHI for this ask.
Tag name phi for PHI tables, applied consistently in CONF-010 and CONF-012 (template default for CONF-012 was confidential).
Org scoping uses the org_id field on patients and users; $auth.org_id is a valid reference on the auth table users.
The tables scope param narrows field_attribute_required and tag_required to the named tables, as the scope section describes.
The customer means HIPAA Security Rule safeguards; the policies relate to them and do not claim compliance.
clinical_notes_POST and patient_id_GET are the PHI-facing endpoints; appointments_GET is the waiting-room endpoint and holds appointment data.
confusions: CONF-012 template fill is tag confidential, but CONF-010's example is phi. The two templates do not agree on the PHI tag name; I picked phi for both and cannot tell whether the catalogue expects one name.

AUTH-030 template params list is_admin, which the workspace lacks; the skill md says to fill from workspace names, but does not say whether a template param naming a missing field is an error or a placeholder. Parse did not warn.

The skill md template table lists fill params (e.g. fields for DATA-010) but the catalogue template rules set object_kinds and other params; I used the catalogue for rule params and the md for fills. Unclear which is authoritative when they differ.

VND-001 needs hosts or providers, and the template gives no default. I left it out instead of picking vendors; it would have been useful to know whether a rule with empty lists is valid (it reports every destination as unreviewed).
Unclear whether db.output_fields_forbidden counts a whole-row db.get (no explicit field list) as fetching ssn. The check text says 'fetch', so I assume yes, but it is a prediction.

Unclear whether scope param tables applies to field-level checks such as table.field_attribute_required as a table selector, or only filters objects. The scope section says objects; I read it as tables.

The skill says a check can name tables by a scope param but object.tagged_table_access reads table_tags; I could not find whether a tag set on a table counts when no tag exists yet (parse warned that phi is on no table, which is the only signal).

How to exempt the public endpoints in AUTH-010 is covered by the public tag, but the workspace's login and health endpoints already carry it; I did not check whether the tag must sit on the endpoint or its api_group.
wished_for: A HIPAA-oriented recipe or template bundle: which templates together cover the Security Rule safeguards most people ask about (access control, audit, transmission, logoff, minimum necessary).
A single list of the PHI-related tags or table tags the template family expects, with one name per concept (phi vs confidential).
A note on whether a template's fill param naming a missing field is a placeholder or an error.
Guidance on vendor allowlist with no approved vendors yet: is a rule with empty hosts valid and what does it report?
Examples of multi-table scoping for field-level checks (tables scope) with a real result, not only the param description.
why_confidence: The policies parse (all 12 exit 0; one rule warning: phi is on no table). They cover the access, logoff, transmission, minimum-necessary and audit parts of the ask, but none of them can say the workspace is HIPAA-safe. Several rules match nothing until tables are tagged phi (CONF-010, CONF-012 judge only once tagging happens); the vendor allowlist, PHI access auditing, retention and the org process are not covered. I did not run xano policy evaluate (forbidden in this run), so every expected finding listed in the reply is a prediction, not an observed result.
